title: Sustainability Intern – Systems Implementation (6months)
description:
**Job Summary:**

Sustainability at Williams-Sonoma, Inc. (WSI) encompasses our environmental and social initiatives. In this position, you will be focused primarily on implementation of a new system to support traceability and reporting. This includes interacting with our supply chain partners in WSI’s key sourcing markets. You will support suppliers to onboard into the system, troubleshoot and review data. You will contribute to the success of WSI's sustainability initiatives through the timely collection, management, and analysis of data from our supply chain partners.

An ideal candidate should have an interest in sustainability technology solutions and be comfortable working with multiple stakeholders. In return, you will be supported by a collaborative and experienced global sustainability dream team!

**This position is a 6-12 months internship position with the possibility to convert to contract.**

**Key responsibilities:**

* Support the WSI Sustainability team in achieving companywide and brand-specific goals related to responsible materials through implementation of a new technology platform for suppliers
* Work with sustainability team to monitor supplier compliance by analyzing vendor cotton supply chain mapping and ensuring alignment with WSI requirements
* Supplier communication about sustainability system purpose & expectations
* Manage system, including resolving vendor issues, providing timely assistance and recommending changes
Monitor supplier compliance - ensure suppliers are submitting data in timely manner through the system’s task function & review submitted data  

**Desired qualifications and competencies:**

* Keen interest in sustainability, supply chain management, or related fields
* Experience in sustainability and traceability projects is an advantage
* Detail oriented with proven analytical skills and experience processing large amounts of data to derive insight and develop recommendations for action
* Maintains a global perspective and is culturally sensitive and aware.
* Demonstrates a creative, energetic and motivated spirit.
* Thrives in a collaborative & diverse team environment.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office Skills (especially Excel)
* Exceptional written and verbal communication skills
* Knowledgeable about Power BI is a plus

**Commitment period:**

* Minimum able to commit to 5 full days a week, ideally for 6-12 months

description:
This course looks at how values connect with finance.  
The first part (7.5 hours) is a one‑day workshop. It has two goals:  

* Finance ethics: learning how to make ethical decisions in finance and beyond.
* Ethical expression: learning practical skills to act on those decisions in the workplace without harming your career.

The second part (7.5 hours) runs over several sessions and introduces the basics of ESG investing (considering environmental, social, and governance factors in investment decisions). We will explore:  

* Why investors care about ESG factors.
* How ESG performance links to financial performance and valuation.
* What the “E” and “S” mean, and how they relate to issues like climate change.
* Why governance (“G”) matters and what organisational questions it raises.
* The main ESG reporting frameworks, and how to spot greenwashing when analysing ESG data.

* Mark Individual or Group Assignment if required.
* Period of teaching: 15 hrs
* To understand the content of the module well, communicate with the module leader to understand the expectations on the module, work closely with UP programme director and module lead on the content for delivery.

title: Associate Lecturer - Fundamentals of Sustainability in Management (HE3)
description:
Job Description

Sustainability is a central and substantive part of the operating environment of all organisations. This module will help you to investigate the foundational concepts, theories, language and tools necessary to understand and enact sustainability within the management of all types of organisations.  
The module focuses on how sustainability (composed of social, environmental and economic) issues shape the way managers make decisions and act within organisations. We will seek to answer three questions: one, what is the state of the world (e.g. climate change, the Anthropocene, planetary boundaries); two, why do we care (e.g. business case for sustainability, legal requirements); three, what can we do about it (e.g. environmental management systems, systems thinking). The module concludes with key tools used by managers to manage sustainability issues.

Requirement:  
Mark Individual or Group Assignment

Job Requirement

* A PHD or Master's Degree in related discipline from a reputable university
* At least 2 years of relevant teaching experience at the tertiary level
* 5 years of relevant work experience will be an added advantage
* Familiar with various referencing styles, especially the Harvard Stirling University Referencing style

description:
**Description**
---------------

**The Business**

The Asia-Pacific Climate Risk Centre is WTW’s focal point for our climate expertise and capabilities in the region. The Centre support clients in developing resilience to climate risks through advisory, transactional, and implementational services. It works across our people, risk and capital businesses to deliver climate and resilience solutions in response to a range of regulatory, investor, consumer, employee and operating pressures.

The Centre is looking for individuals with a talent for independent thinking, effective collaboration and pragmatic problem-solving skills.

**The Role**

As a Climate Risk Consultant, you will work with a variety of clients that are exposed to climate risk, including public listed and large private companies, as well as governments and development banks. You will identify and quantify climate risk, and design risk management and financing strategies. You will be involved in many aspects of such advice, from risk quantification to mitigation and risk financing design, and ensure the analysis undertaken is policy and business relevant.

You will be entering our Asia-Pacific Climate Risk Centre, with scope to contribute to its development.

Day to day tasks will include:

* Use of WTW climate risk models to understand current and evolving risks for clients, and research to support delivery of projects.
* Innovation on climate-related insurance products (including parametric, insurance-linked securities, carbon).
* Relationship building with clients on climate risks and climate risk management, and ongoing engagement and support.
* Be an internal champion for climate risks and innovative insurance.
* Produce high-quality materials such as numerical analysis, written documents and presentations to short deadlines

**Qualifications**
------------------

* An insightful, independent, analytical mind, with a passion for climate change issues.
* Ability to reveal insights from quantitative and qualitative datasets.
* Strong awareness of the evolving climate and sustainability agenda in Asia.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to communicate methods, results and recommendations from complex analysis to expert and non-technical audiences.
* Degree in climate change, environmental science/economics, business / management, or other academic field relevant to climate change.
* Self-starter, ability to juggle multiple complex tasks at the same time.
* Professionalism, enthusiasm for working as part of a team, and ability to interact with a diverse group of people
